+Description: Learn how permanent residents can apply for Australian citizenship and meet residency and eligibility requirements.
 Become an Australian citizen (by conferral)
 Permanent residents including New Zealand Special Category visa (SCV) holders
 Becoming a citizen by conferral is a common way to become an Australian citizen. You need to be a permanent resident and meet certain criteria before you can apply.
@@ -57,7 +57,7 @@
 We must be satisfied that you are likely to live or continue to live in Australia, or maintain a close and continuing link with Australia while overseas. Citizenship is a privilege that requires a long-term commitment to Australia. A close and continuing association with family or other social relationships in Australia, including people who are Australian citizens, may not be sufficient to be considered as having a close and continuing link to Australia on its own. When we assess your close and continuing link to Australia, we will consider your living arrangements and migration status, including: if you rent or own property and where this property is located if you have high value items and where these are located, such as a house, property, car or bank account any commitments or ties to Australia, such as your source of income, employment situation, family situation, and schooling arrangements your travel into and out of Australia, your reason for travel, the number of times you travelled into and out of Australia, and how long you were in each place participation in the Australian community, such as being part of community groups, clubs or charities that provides services or opportunities if you have close Australian permanent resident or citizen family members who intend to reside in Australia, such as a spouse, de facto partner or child/ren. For information on the supporting documents we require, see Evidence of close and continuing link to Australia.
 We cannot approve your application in certain circumstances
 We must not approve your citizenship application if we are not satisfied of your identity. Identity is assessed from birth.
-We must not approve your application for Australian citizenship: • when proceedings for an offence against an Australian law (including proceedings by way of appeal or review) are pending. • when it is less than 2 years since you were released from prison after serving a prison sentence of 12 months or more, or 10 years if you are a repeat offender. • you are subject to certain conditions set by an Australian court (such as being released on parole, good behaviour or bail) where action may be taken against you for breach of those conditions. • you are in prison or a psychiatric institution by order of the court at the time of decision
+We must not approve your application for Australian citizenship: when proceedings for an offence against an Australian law (including proceedings by way of appeal or review) are pending. when it is less than 2 years since you were released from prison after serving a prison sentence of 12 months or more, or 10 years if you are a repeat offender. you are subject to certain conditions set by an Australian court (such as being released on parole, good behaviour or bail) where action may be taken against you for breach of those conditions. you are in prison or a psychiatric institution by order of the court at the time of decision.
 Risk to National security
 We must not approve your citizenship application if you are assessed as a risk to the security of Australia.
 We must not approve your citizenship application if you ceased to be an Australian citizen in the past 12 months.

The work needs to be in the same field we granted the visa for and in one of the following areas: academia and research the arts a profession a sport. work as a minister of religion in a senior leadership position role in a religious organisation. Work includes activities done while performing: senior religious leadership and pastoral duties; or executive governance or administrative functions of the religious organisation; or ceremonial, representative or community engagement duties completed while a minister of religion in a senior leadership position. Evidence of kind of work and regular travel outside Australia because of employment Documents from your employer showing that when you applied and for a period of 2 years in the past 4 years, you worked in one of the specified kinds of work listed below. This must show that the work needed regular travel outside Australia. Examples include: letter from employer employment contracts pay slips logbooks overseas meeting and conference agendas with dates of the meetings invitations to present at conferences overseas shift-work schedules with dates worked. The documents must also show that the periods spent outside Australia during that two-year period were for that work. Chief executive officer or executive manager of an S&P/ASX All Australian 200 listed company Along with evidence of the kind of work and regular travel outside Australia because of employment, also give us: evidence that states that you work for a S&P/ASX All Australian 200 listed company. This needs to be as a chief executive officer or executive manager, and for executive managers, evidence that confirms you report directly to the most senior person in the company. Scientist or academic completing research and development of benefit to Australia, awarded a Doctor of Philosophy in their field of speciality and employed by an Australian university Along with evidence of the kind of work and regular travel outside Australia because of employment, also give us evidence that: you hold a Doctor of Philosophy in the field of speciality of your work with an Australian university, and the research and development you are completing with an Australian university is of benefit to Australia. This may include: published articles/work in peer reviewed journals or books evidence you get funding from an Australian body for this research. if you are a scientist, evidence from the Australian university employing you to confirm your employment as a scientist. You must be qualified in one of the following branches of science: natural social formal. if you are an academic, evidence from the Australian university employing you to confirm your employment as an academic and the discipline in which you are qualified. Scientist (CSIRO) or medical research institute member of AAMRI Along with evidence of the kind of work and regular travel outside Australia because of employment, also give us: evidence from the CSIRO or AAMRI that they consider you a scientist qualified in one of the following branches of science: natural social formal. Medical specialist internationally renowned in their field, who: is a fellow of an organisation listed in column 1 of an item in the table in clause 1 in Schedule 1 to the Health Insurance Regulations 2018 and holds a qualification relevant to the organisation. Along with evidence of the kind of work and regular travel outside Australia because of employment types above, also give us: evidence that you hold a qualification relevant to the organisation you work for, and evidence of international recognition of exceptional and outstanding achievement in your field of work as a medical specialist. This may include but is not limited to: written work for internationally renowned journals papers presented at international conferences in your field of expertise work as an international consultant with universities or hospitals.
